questions.q: What is Unified Auditing, per this lesson?
options: The default, consolidated auditing mechanism in Oracle 12c and later, replacing three previously fragmented mechanisms
A separate OS-level tool unrelated to the database
A synonym for Virtual Private Database
A feature only available for SYS actions
questions.explain: Unified Auditing consolidates standard auditing, fine-grained auditing, and OS-level auditing output into one audit trail.

questions.q: Where do Unified Auditing records end up, queryable as a normal view?
options: unified_audit_trail
SYS.AUD$ only, with no view available
The Windows Application log
DBMS_RLS.ADD_POLICY
questions.explain: unified_audit_trail is the consolidated view exposing all unified audit records.

questions.q: What distinguishes Fine-Grained Auditing (DBMS_FGA) from standard/unified auditing on a table?
options: FGA only writes an audit record when a specific condition or column is actually touched, instead of recording every matching action
FGA works only on the SYS schema
FGA replaces the need for a policy entirely
FGA can only audit DELETE statements
questions.explain: FGA narrows WHEN a record is written, e.g. only when a query touches the SALARY column, rather than every access.

questions.q: What does a Virtual Private Database (VPD) policy actually do to a query?
options: Transparently rewrites the query to add a WHERE predicate, enforced at the database level and unbypassable by the application
Blocks the query from running at all if it doesn't include a WHERE clause
Only logs the query for later review
Encrypts the columns referenced in the query
questions.explain: VPD, via DBMS_RLS, injects a predicate from a policy function into every query against the protected object.

questions.q: A requirement states: 'the query should never even return other regions' rows.' Which tool from this lesson actually satisfies that?
options: Virtual Private Database (VPD) — auditing only records access, it doesn't restrict what a query returns
Unified Auditing, since it records every row accessed
Fine-Grained Auditing, since it can be configured to block rows
PASSWORD_VERIFY_FUNCTION, since it enforces access rules
questions.explain: Auditing (unified or fine-grained) only records what happened after the fact; VPD is the tool that actually restricts what rows a query can return.
